narrative: A user opened a Microsoft Word attachment from a phishing email and enabled macros. The macro executed commands to download and run additional malware from a remote server.
provenance: Based on CISA AA20-227A (2020) describing phishing emails with malicious VBA macros deploying KONNI malware; rewritten as a short, generic summary. CISA advisories are U.S. government works and in the public domain.

narrative: Attackers gained access to a Windows server and used PowerShell commands to download and execute Cobalt Strike Beacon malware from their command-and-control infrastructure.
provenance: Based on CISA AA25-050A (2025) describing Ghost ransomware actors using PowerShell to download and execute Cobalt Strike; rewritten as a short, generic summary. CISA advisories are U.S. government works and in the public domain.

narrative: Phishing emails delivered Word documents with embedded macros. When enabled, the macros invoked scripts to download additional payloads and spread laterally using brute-force credential guessing.
provenance: Based on CISA AA20-280A (2020) describing Emotet distribution via phishing attachments and macro-enabled documents; rewritten as a short, generic summary. CISA advisories are U.S. government works and in the public domain.

narrative: Threat actors performed brute-force attacks against exposed Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) services. After obtaining valid credentials, they logged in and deployed ransomware across the network.
provenance: Synthetic narrative reflecting common RDP brute-force and ransomware patterns described in multiple CISA ransomware advisories; not derived from any single copyrighted source.

narrative: Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in an on-premises SharePoint server to upload a malicious web shell. They then used PowerShell to run commands and move laterally within the environment.
provenance: Inspired by CISA alerts on SharePoint exploitation chains (e.g., 2025 advisories on ToolShell); rewritten as a short, generic summary. CISA advisories are U.S. government works and in the public domain.
